# Answer key: python-core

Area: the Python package and its tests in `sample-app/` (`app/`, `tests/`, `README.md`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt`).
Paths below are relative to `sample-app/`. Line numbers are from the committed fixture.

Baseline: `cd sample-app && python -m pytest -q` gives **1 failed, 18 passed**. The only failure is
`tests/test_batches.py::test_paginate_returns_requested_page` (PY-02). `python -m pyflakes app tests`
reports only the four unused imports in `app/utils.py` (PY-29). `python -m mccabe --min 8` flags only
`app/report.py::site_summary` (complexity 21, PY-19).

## Seeded defects

| ID | File | Function / line | Category | Description | Correct fix |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PY-01 | app/batches.py | `list_batches`, L38 and L40 | security: SQL injection | `product` and `site` are put into the SQL with f-strings (`f"product = '{product}'"`), and `api.py` passes them straight from the query string, so `?site=x' OR '1'='1` returns every batch. | Use placeholders for these two filters as the `status` filter already does: `clauses.append("product = ?"); params.append(product)`, and the same for `site`. |
| PY-02 | app/batches.py | `paginate`, L72-73 | correctness: off-by-one | For 1-based pages it computes `start = (page - 1) * page_size + 1` and `end = page * page_size`, so it drops the first item of every page and returns `page_size - 1` items (`paginate(range(1,11),1,3)` gives `[2, 3]`). This makes `test_paginate_returns_requested_page` fail, and `GET /batches` loses one row per page. | `start = (page - 1) * page_size`, `end = start + page_size`, then return `items[start:end]`. |
| PY-03 | app/batches.py | `batches_with_materials`, L51-65 | performance: N+1 query | Runs one `SELECT` for the batches and then one `SELECT ... FROM materials WHERE batch_id = ?` per batch inside the loop, so N batches cost 1+N queries. | Load all materials in one query (`JOIN`, or `WHERE batch_id IN (...)` / a subquery on the same status filter), group them in Python by `batch_id`, then attach each group to its batch. |
| PY-04 | app/__init__.py | L9 `SECRET_KEY`, L14 `LIMS_API_TOKEN` | security: hardcoded secret | The app secret key and a live-looking LIMS bearer token are string literals in source control. Next to them, `DB_PATH` and `LIMS_BASE_URL` are read from the environment. | Read both from the environment or a secret store (`os.environ["BATCHTRACK_SECRET_KEY"]`, `os.environ["BATCHTRACK_LIMS_TOKEN"]`) and fail fast when they are missing. Rotate the exposed values. Either literal alone counts as finding PY-04. |
| PY-05 | app/batches.py | `set_actual_qty`, L91-103 | resource: connection leak | Opens `db.connect(db_path)` and calls `conn.close()` only on the success path (L103). The `LookupError` (L97), the `ValueError` (L99), a `ValueError` from `normalize_batch_no`, and any SQL error all leave the connection open. | Use the existing `with db.session(db_path) as conn:` context manager, or wrap the body in `try/finally: conn.close()`. |
| PY-06 | app/users.py | `hash_password`, L10 | security: weak password hashing | Passwords are hashed with a single unsalted MD5 (`hashlib.md5(pw).hexdigest()`). This is fast to brute-force, open to rainbow tables, and equal passwords give equal hashes. | Use a salted, slow KDF: `hashlib.scrypt` or `hashlib.pbkdf2_hmac("sha256", pw, salt, >=600_000)` with a random per-user `os.urandom(16)` salt stored with the hash (or bcrypt/argon2), and migrate existing hashes on next login. |
| PY-07 | app/users.py | `verify_password`, L44 | security: timing-unsafe comparison | Compares the stored and computed hashes with `==`, which short-circuits and leaks timing information. | `hmac.compare_digest(stored, computed)` (and verify through the KDF from PY-06). |
| PY-08 | app/signatures.py | `sign_batch`, L8 / L15 (and `api.py` L83) | GxP / 21 CFR Part 11: signature time source | The signature timestamp `signed_at` comes from the caller (`data["signed_at"]` in the POST body), so signatures can be backdated or future-dated. Part 11 §11.50 requires the date and time of signing. | Ignore any client value and set `signed_at = utils.utc_now_iso()` on the server inside `sign_batch`. Remove the parameter. |
| PY-09 | app/signatures.py | `update_signature`, L30-45 | GxP / Part 11: audit trail | Overwrites `meaning` and `signed_at` on an existing signature row in place (`UPDATE signatures SET ...`) and writes no `audit_log` entry, so the original value is lost. §11.10(e) requires a secure audit trail with the old and new values. | Executed signatures should not be edited. Reject the change, or record a new superseding signature. At minimum, read the old row and call `db.write_audit(..., "update", old, new, user_id)` in the same transaction, with the acting user passed in. |
| PY-10 | app/signatures.py | `delete_signature`, L48-50 | GxP / Part 11: audit trail | Hard-deletes a signature with no audit record and no record of who deleted it. | Do not physically delete. Mark it void or withdrawn with a reason and user, and write an `audit_log` row (`action="delete"`, old value = the row as JSON, `user_id`). |
| PY-11 | app/signatures.py | `sign_batch` `meaning=None`, L8 / L15 | GxP / Part 11: signature manifestation | The signature meaning is optional, defaults to `None`, is stored as NULL, and is never checked against a controlled list. §11.50(a)(3) requires the meaning (for example review, approval, responsibility). | Make `meaning` required and check it against an allowed set (for example `{"performed", "reviewed", "approved"}`). Raise `ValueError` otherwise. Make the column `NOT NULL`. |
| PY-12 | app/signatures.py | `sign_batch` signature (no credentials), L8; `api.py` L80-84 | GxP / Part 11: re-authentication | Signing takes only a `user_id` (sent by the client in the POST body). No password or second credential is checked when signing. §11.200(a) requires both components (ID and password) at signing, and at least the password for later signings in the same session. | Require the signer's credentials at signing: call `users.authenticate(conn, username, password)`, sign as the authenticated user's id (never a client-supplied `user_id`), and reject the signature if authentication fails. |
| PY-13 | app/cache.py | `get_batch` L27-34 and `invalidate` L37-39 | concurrency: check-then-act race | `if batch_no in _cache and not _expired(...)`, then `_cache[batch_no]`, and `if batch_no in _cache: del _cache[batch_no]` are unsynchronised check-then-act on a module-level dict shared by `warm_cache`'s `ThreadPoolExecutor`. A concurrent `invalidate` gives `KeyError`, and concurrent misses load the same key several times (verified: 200 lookups of 1 key with 16 workers gave 2-13 misses across runs instead of 1). The `_lock` exists but only `clear()` uses it. | Hold `_lock` around lookup, insert and invalidate (load outside the lock or use per-key locks/futures), use `_cache.get()` / `_cache.pop(key, None)`, or replace with `functools.lru_cache` or a small thread-safe cache class. |
| PY-14 | app/cache.py | `get_batch` L29 and L31 | concurrency: non-atomic counter | `_stats["hits"] += 1` / `_stats["misses"] += 1` are read-modify-write from multiple threads with no lock, so updates can be lost (guaranteed on free-threaded builds). | Increment under `_lock` (or use `itertools.count` / per-thread counters). |
| PY-15 | app/lims_client.py | `_request`, L20 | reliability: missing timeout | `urllib.request.urlopen(req)` is called with no `timeout`, so a hung LIMS blocks the calling thread (and an API request) indefinitely. | `urlopen(req, timeout=10)` (make it configurable). |
| PY-16 | app/lims_client.py | `_send`, L24-31 | reliability: retry without backoff | Retries up to 3 times immediately with no delay or jitter. It also retries `HTTPError` (a `URLError` subclass), which includes 4xx client errors. | Use exponential backoff with jitter (`time.sleep(base * 2**attempt + random.uniform(0, base))`), retry only on connection errors, timeouts and 5xx/429, and re-raise 4xx at once. |
| PY-17 | app/lims_client.py | `submit_sample` L47 via `_send` | reliability: non-idempotent retry | `submit_sample` sends `POST /samples` through the same retry loop. If the server created the sample but the response was lost, the retry creates a duplicate QC sample. | Do not retry POST automatically, or send an idempotency key (for example a header derived from batch, lot and tests, or a client UUID) that the server de-duplicates on. Only retry idempotent methods by default. |
| PY-18 | app/lims_client.py | `get_sample_results`, L40-41 | error handling: swallowed exception | `except Exception: pass` hides every failure (network, HTTP 401/5xx, bad JSON, an unexpected payload shape) and returns `None`. `is_lot_approved` then reports "not approved" when the real problem is "LIMS unreachable", and nothing is logged. | Catch only the expected errors, log them, and raise a domain error (for example `LimsUnavailable`) or return an explicit result. Never let the function fall through to an implicit `None`. |
| PY-19 | app/report.py | `site_summary`, L21-81 | maintainability: complexity | One 60-line function with cyclomatic complexity 21 and nesting up to 5 levels. Status branching, per-product statistics, low/high yield flags and a post-processing pass are all inline, with repeated `append({...})` blocks. | Split into helpers (`_new_site_entry`, `_update_product_stats(stats, pct)`, `_yield_flag(row, pct, low, high)`, `_finalise(entry)`), use `setdefault` or `defaultdict`, and collapse the duplicated low/high append branches (the flag is just `row["status"]` for non-released rows). |
| PY-20 | app/report.py | `collect_warnings(rows, warnings=[])`, L12 | correctness: mutable default argument | The default list is created once and appended to on every call, so warnings pile up across calls (and across `build_report` calls, which use the default). | `def collect_warnings(rows, warnings=None):` then `warnings = [] if warnings is None else warnings`. |
| PY-21 | app/report.py | `_percentile`, L84-91 | dead code | A private helper that is never referenced anywhere in the repo. | Delete it, or use it (for example for a p10/p90 yield band in `site_summary`) and add a test. |
| PY-22 | app/report.py | `yield_pct`, L9 (reached from `site_summary` L40) | correctness: division by zero | `actual_qty / planned_qty` raises `ZeroDivisionError` when `planned_qty` is 0 (and `TypeError` when it is NULL). One such batch crashes the whole `build_report`. | Guard it: `if not planned_qty: return None` (callers then skip it or add it to warnings), or check `planned_qty > 0` when the batch is created. |
| PY-23 | app/report.py | whole module | test coverage gap | `report.py` has no tests (no `tests/test_report.py`, nothing imports `app.report`), even though it holds the yield maths and the defects above. | Add `tests/test_report.py` covering `yield_pct` (including 0 planned), `collect_warnings` called twice, `site_summary` flags and averages, `format_report`, and `build_report` on the `conn` fixture. |
| PY-24 | app/api.py | `do_GET` `/batches/<id>/release`, L57-60 | API design: unsafe GET | A GET request releases a batch (`batches.release_batch`, which changes `status` and writes the audit log). Crawlers, prefetchers, link previews or a browser refresh can release batches, and CSRF becomes trivial. | Move it to `POST` (or `PUT/PATCH /batches/<id>` with `{"status": "released"}`), require an authenticated user, and keep GET handlers read-only. |
| PY-25 | app/api.py | `_send(status=200)` L24; error sends L54, L64, L73, L87 | API design: wrong status codes | Every error (not found, bad input, unknown route) is returned with HTTP **200** and a body `{"error": ...}`, so clients and monitoring see success. | Return proper codes: 404 for unknown batch or route, 400/422 for invalid input, 405 for wrong method (for example `self._send({...}, status=404)`). |
| PY-26 | app/api.py | `_summary` L10-18 vs `do_GET` detail L56; POST bodies L71 vs L83 | API design: inconsistent naming | The list endpoint returns camelCase (`batchNo`, `plannedQty`), but `GET /batches/<id>` returns the raw row in snake_case (`batch_no`, `planned_qty`). `POST /batches` expects `batchNo`/`plannedQty`, while `POST /batches/<id>/signatures` expects `user_id`/`signed_at` and returns `signature_id`. | Pick one convention (for example snake_case everywhere, or camelCase at the API boundary), serialise every response through one mapper, and accept the same convention on input. |
| PY-27 | app/api.py | `int(parts[1])` at L52, L58, L62, L83; `int(query...)` L49, L59 | input validation | Path ids and query numbers are passed to `int()` unchecked. `/batches/abc` raises an uncaught `ValueError`, the handler dies, and the client gets a dropped connection (verified: `RemoteDisconnected`). Negative or zero ids and `page=0` also go through unchecked, and `release_batch` raises an uncaught `LookupError` for unknown ids. | Validate with a regex or `str.isdigit()` and a positive-range check before converting, and return 400 on bad input and 404 on unknown ids. Catch domain exceptions in one place and map them to status codes. |
| PY-28 | app/utils.py | `clean_batch_no`, L18-23 (+ `_BATCH_NO` L10) | maintainability: duplicated logic | Copies `batches.normalize_batch_no` / `BATCH_NO_RE` (same strip/upper/remove-spaces steps and the same regex). `api.py` calls one and then `create_batch` calls the other, so the two can drift. | Keep one implementation (for example `batches.normalize_batch_no`, or move it to utils and import it in batches) and delete the other. Point `api.py` at it. |
| PY-29 | app/utils.py | L3 `hashlib`, L4 `json`, L5 `os`, L7 `defaultdict` | maintainability: unused imports | Four imports that are never used (pyflakes F401). | Remove them. |
| PY-30 | tests/test_batches.py | `test_batches_with_materials_is_fast`, L42-45 | test quality: flaky timing test | Asserts wall-clock time `< 0.01`s for a DB call. It passes locally (about 20 µs) but can fail on a loaded CI runner, during GC, or under coverage or debuggers. It does not actually test the N+1 behaviour. | Remove the timing assertion. To guard against N+1, count queries instead (`conn.set_trace_callback`) and assert the number stays constant as the batch count grows, or move it to a separate benchmark suite. |
| PY-31 | tests/test_batches.py | `test_release_batch`, L60-62 | test quality: no assertion | Calls `create_batch` and `release_batch` but asserts nothing, so it passes whatever `release_batch` does (short of raising). | Assert the return value (`is True`), that `get_batch(...)["status"] == "released"`, and that a second call returns `False`. | PY-32 | tests/test_users.py | `test_authenticate_returns_user_for_valid_credentials` L30-34, `test_verify_password_rejects_wrong_password` L37-41, `test_hash_password_differs_per_password` L44-46 | test quality: over-mocking | Each test patches **the function under test itself** (`app.users.authenticate`, `users.verify_password`, `users.hash_password`) and then asserts on the mock's canned return, so no production code runs. These tests would pass even if the real functions were deleted or broken. | Remove the patches and call the real functions against the `conn` fixture: `authenticate(conn, "alice", "Alice#2026qa")` returns alice's dict, a wrong password returns `None`, `verify_password(find_user(conn, "bob"), "wrong")` is `False`, and hashes differ per password (and, after PY-06, per salt). Mock only real external boundaries. |

Notes for graders:
- For PY-02, the agent should point to the slice in `paginate`, not to the test. The correct fix makes all 19 tests pass except the timing-dependent PY-30 (which normally passes).
- For PY-08 to PY-12, credit a finding that names the specific function and the specific control (time source, audit trail on update, audit trail on delete, meaning, re-authentication). A generic "not Part 11 compliant" with no specifics earns no credit.
- PY-16 and PY-17 are separate: no backoff/jitter (or retrying 4xx) is PY-16, and retrying a non-idempotent POST is PY-17.
- PY-13 and PY-14 are separate: check-then-act on the dict is PY-13, and the unsynchronised counter increment is PY-14.

## False-positive traps (correct code; reporting these as defects is a false positive)

| ID | File | Location | Why it is correct |
|---|---|---|---|
| FP-01 | app/users.py | `find_user` L26-30 and `list_users` L33-40 | Every value is bound with `?` placeholders. `list_users` builds SQL with `sql += " WHERE role = ?"` and `" ORDER BY username"`, but only constant fragments are joined and `role` is passed in `params`. **This is not SQL injection.** |
| FP-02 | app/signatures.py | `update_signature` L43 `f"UPDATE signatures SET {', '.join(fields)} WHERE id = ?"` | The f-string only joins fixed strings chosen by code (`"meaning = ?"`, `"signed_at = ?"`), and all values are bound parameters. **This is not SQL injection.** (The function *is* defective for the audit reason, PY-09. Only an injection claim here is a false positive.) |
| FP-03 | app/batches.py | `list_batches` L41-43 (`status` filter) | `status` is correctly parameterised (`"status = ?"` plus `params.append`). Only `product`/`site` are injectable (PY-01). A finding that says all three filters are injectable is only partly right. |
| FP-04 | app/db.py | `session()` L71-82 | This context manager commits on success, rolls back on exception, and closes in `finally`. It is correct. Contrast it with PY-05. |
| FP-05 | app/lims_client.py | `get_sample_results` L36 `urllib.parse.urlencode({"lot": lot_no})` | The query string is correctly encoded, so this is not URL or parameter injection. |
| FP-06 | app/cache.py | `clear()` L61-65 | This takes `_lock` correctly. Only `get_batch`/`invalidate` and the counters are racy. |
| FP-07 | app/report.py | `site_summary` L78 `entry["released"] / entry["batches"]` and `stats()` in cache.py L56 | Both divisions are guarded (`if entry["batches"]`, `if total`). The only unguarded division is `yield_pct` (PY-22). |
| FP-08 | app/users.py | `create_user` L13-23 | Validation of role and minimum password length is correct, and the insert is parameterised. The only problem here is the hash function it calls (PY-06). |
| FP-09 | app/lims_client.py | `is_lot_approved` L51-53 | `bool(results) and all(...)` correctly refuses to approve a lot with no results (avoids vacuous `all([]) == True`). |
| FP-10 | public functions in `app/` that nothing inside `app/` calls: `users.authenticate`, `users.create_user`, `users.list_users`, `batches.batches_with_materials`, `batches.set_actual_qty`, `signatures.update_signature`, `signatures.delete_signature`, `cache.invalidate`, `cache.warm_cache`, `cache.clear`, `lims_client.submit_sample`, `lims_client.is_lot_approved`, `report.build_report` | These are the package's public API (several are used by the tests). Calling any of them dead code is a false positive. Only the private `report._percentile` is dead code (PY-21). |

## Other legitimate observations (not seeded; do not count against the agent, do not require them)

- `api.py` has no authentication or authorisation at all. `release` takes `user_id` from the query string, and signing takes `user_id` from the JSON body (this overlaps PY-12 and PY-24).
- `batches.release_batch` does not check for a QA "approved" signature before releasing (a GMP business-rule gap).
- `api.py` `_read_json` does not handle malformed JSON or a missing `user_id`/`signed_at` (`KeyError`), so both crash the handler (related to PY-27).
- `users.authenticate` returns faster for unknown usernames than for wrong passwords (username enumeration by timing, related to PY-07).
- `create_batch` allows `planned_qty` of `None`, 0 or a negative value (the root cause of PY-22 data).
- Long lines (>100 characters) in `report.py`, and unused loop variables (`site`, `product`) in `site_summary`'s final pass.
